_meta.purpose: Classify every maintained file under data/ by provenance type, including the 2026-09-06 provenance cleanup, without inventing missing lineage.
_meta.coverageRule: Every maintained file under data/ is listed except this classification manifest itself. New data files must be classified before release QA can pass.

interpretation.project-authored/manual: Project-created rules, corrections or metadata with no claimed copied external dataset.
interpretation.externally-derived: Data or metadata selected, transformed or generated from an identified external source.
interpretation.mixed: Project curation combines external evidence with manual decisions or multiple source families so no single upstream snapshot fully describes the file.
interpretation.legacy/unknown: The current project cannot establish a reliable source basis. No file is assigned this category in version 1.

sourceBasis: Compact CJ2R-derived positive Japanese-use scope evidence from selected factual fields in MJ文字情報一覧表 Ver.006.02; the full MJ source workbook is not redistributed.
Stable Unicode Unihan 18.0.0 Japanese-specific kJapanese/kJapaneseOn/kMojiJoho/kIRG_JSource properties are used only as secondary corroboration; Chinese/Korean readings are excluded.

For the rare U+3106C Japanese-created/transmitted ghost-character, Japanese scholarly and National Diet Library reference evidence records たいと・だいと・おとど while explicitly preserving the disputed historicity/actual surname-use caveat.

Runtime policy may resolve an exact single Han character only when the reviewed Japanese-scope bank contains exactly one Japanese reading; multiple legitimate readings remain candidate provenance and require review.

The 2026-09-11 Batch 2 follow-up researched the complete 269-character unknown-scope set before implementation; 256 characters gained positive Japanese reading evidence and 13 were retained as unknown.

Japanese-language dictionary and character-infrastructure evidence is primary for this review. Component names are not treated as standalone readings, explicitly unknown readings remain unknown, and provisional/convenience readings are not promoted.

Where Unicode Japanese-specific properties conflict with stronger Japanese lexicographic evidence, the Japanese lexicographic evidence governs; 炻 is recorded as セキ rather than importing the conflicting Unicode value.
